$comment: Corrections that outrank every source, and the only data here a rebuild cannot re-derive.
Everything else in this project comes from GeoNames, dr5hn, Wikidata or CLDR and is
disposable: re-run the ETL and it returns the same or better. These do not. The knowledge
that Brazil's state of Acre is not the unit of area exists nowhere upstream, so if it is
not written down here it is lost on the next run.
Add one when a source is wrong, not when it is merely absent. A missing name is reported
honestly as `romanised` and may arrive upstream next month; a wrong name is served to a
reader as though it were right, and will not fix itself.
Every entry needs a `why`. An override with no reason is indistinguishable from a typo
six months later, and the person who has to decide whether to keep it will not be you.

subdivision:BR-AC.why: dr5hn machine-translated the state name as the unit of area. エーカー and فدان both mean 'acre' the measurement. The place is a transliteration of the Portuguese.
